scenarios.title: Overcurrent with the temperature sensor frozen
scenarios.description: The current limit is pushed up while the pack-temp reading is pinned low, so the BMS never derates — the pack overheats.
scenarios.consequence: a reading is pinned to a safe-looking value while the process drifts

scenarios.title: Temperature reading drifts low while current is forced up
scenarios.description: The reported pack temperature slides 0.01 °C lower every second at 210 A — no single reading looks wrong, but the BMS derates too late and the pack overheats.
scenarios.consequence: a reading slides away from reality too slowly for any one frame to look wrong

scenarios.title: Last good temperature frame replayed
scenarios.description: The last good pack-temperature frame is replayed forever at 220 A, so the gauge freezes while the real pack heats behind it.
scenarios.consequence: the last good reading is replayed while the real process keeps moving

scenarios.title: Fabricated temperature curve, 15 °C low
scenarios.description: A fake reading rises exactly as Joule heating predicts but sits 15 °C below reality at 230 A; only the absolute physics model sees the offset.
scenarios.consequence: a fabricated curve with real dynamics hides an absolute offset

scenarios.title: Mass max-power command to every charger
scenarios.description: All chargers are commanded to maximum at once; the shared transformer overloads.
scenarios.consequence: many devices driven at once past an aggregate limit
